L257: 
L258: Added in `1.2`
L259: 
L260: Tasks allow you to form dependencies between code, executed in parallel.
L261: ## Defining tasks
L262: 
L263: devenv.nix
L264: 
L265:     `{ pkgs, ... }:
L266: 
L267:     {
L268:       tasks."myapp:hello" = {
L269:         exec = ''echo "Hello, world!"'';
L270:       };
L271:     }
L272:     `
L273: 
L274:     `$ devenv tasks run myapp:hello
L275:     Running tasks     myapp:hello
L276:     Succeeded         myapp:hello         9ms
L277:     1 Succeeded                           10.14ms
L278:     `
L279: 
L280: Added in `1.7`
L281: You can also run all tasks in a namespace by providing just the namespace prefix:
L282: 
L283:     `$ devenv tasks run myapp
L284:     Running tasks     myapp:hello myapp:build myapp:test
L285:     Succeeded         myapp:hello           9ms
L286:     Succeeded         myapp:build         120ms
L287:     Succeeded         myapp:test          350ms
L288:     3 Succeeded                           479.14ms
L289:     `
L290: ## Dependencies between tasks
L291: 
L292: Tasks form a dependency graph (a DAG). Declare an edge between two tasks with `before` or `after`:
L293: 
L294:   * `after = [ "other" ]` — run this task after `other` (`other` is a dependency, "upstream").
L295:   * `before = [ "other" ]` — run this task before `other` (`other` is "downstream" and depends on this one).
L296: Processes are tasks too (see cite147†Processes as tasks ), so the same `before`/`after` edges connect tasks and processes interchangeably — see cite190†process dependencies for process-focused examples.
L297: 
L298: `before` and `after` describe the same edge from opposite ends, so you can declare a dependency from whichever side is more convenient. These are equivalent:
L299: devenv.nix
L300: 
L301:     `{
L302:       # declared from the dependent task
L303:       tasks."myapp:build".after = [ "myapp:generate" ];
L304: 
L305:       # ...is the same edge as declaring it from the dependency
L306:       tasks."myapp:generate".before = [ "myapp:build" ];
L307:     }
L308:     `
L309: ### Dependency states
L310: 
L311: New in version 2.0
L312: 
L313: A dependency waits for its target to reach a particular state before it is considered satisfied. Append an `@` suffix to choose the state explicitly:
L314: Suffix  | Satisfied when  | Failure propagates?
L315: --- | --- | ---
L316: `@started`  | the target has begun executing  | yes
L317: `@ready`  | a process passes its cite191†readiness probe ; for oneshot tasks this means success  | yes
L318: `@succeeded`  | the target exits with code `0` (or is skipped)  | yes
L319: `@completed`  | the target finishes, regardless of exit code  | no (soft dependency)
L320: 
L321: When no suffix is given the default is `@ready` for processes and `@succeeded` for oneshot tasks.
L322: A common use is running a setup task once a service is ready:
L323: 
L324: devenv.nix
L325: 
L326:     `{
L327:       tasks."myapp:configure" = {
L328:         exec = "create-buckets";
L329:         after = [ "devenv:processes:garage@ready" ];
L330:       };
L331:     }
L332:     `
L333: ## Execution modes
L334: 
L335: New in version 2.1
L336: 
L337: When you run a task, devenv schedules a subgraph around it rather than only that one task. `--mode` controls how much of the graph is included:
L338: Mode  | Runs
L339: --- | ---
L340: `single`  | only the named task
L341: `before` (default)  | the task and everything upstream of it (its dependencies)
L342: `after`  | the task and everything downstream of it (tasks that depend on it)
L343: `all`  | the entire connected graph, both upstream and downstream
L344: 
L345:     `$ devenv tasks run myapp:build               # before mode (default): build + its dependencies
L346:     $ devenv tasks run myapp:build --mode single # just build
L347:     $ devenv tasks run myapp:build --mode all    # build, its dependencies, and its dependents
L348:     `
L349: `devenv up` starts processes in `before` mode, while `devenv test` runs in `all` mode. This difference matters for setup tasks attached to processes — see cite147†Processes as tasks .
L350: ## enterShell / enterTest
L351: 
L352: `devenv:enterShell` and `devenv:enterTest` are built-in lifecycle events that run setup tasks at specific points:
L353: 
L354:   * `devenv:enterShell` runs before the shell is entered (`devenv shell`) and before processes start (`devenv up`).
L355:   * `devenv:enterTest` runs before tests execute (`devenv test`). It depends on `devenv:enterShell`, so all shell setup tasks run first automatically.
L356: To hook into these events, use `before` to declare that your task should run before the event completes:
L357: devenv.nix
L358: 
L359:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L360: 
L361:     {
L362:       tasks = {
L363:         "bash:hello" = {
L364:           exec = "echo 'Hello world from bash!'";
L365:           before = [ "devenv:enterShell" ];
L366:         };
L367: 
L368:         "myapp:test-setup" = {
L369:           exec = "echo 'Preparing test fixtures...'";
L370:           before = [ "devenv:enterTest" ];
L371:         };
L372:       };
L373:     }
L374:     `
L375: 
L376:     `$ devenv shell
L377:     ...
L378:     Running tasks     devenv:enterShell
L379:     Succeeded         devenv:git-hooks:install  25ms
L380:     Succeeded         bash:hello                 9ms
L381:     Succeeded         devenv:enterShell         13ms
L382:     3 Succeeded                                 28.14ms
L383:     `
L384: Many devenv modules automatically hook into these events. For example, enabling git hooks registers `devenv:git-hooks:install` as a dependency of `devenv:enterShell`.
L385: ## Using your favourite language
L386: 
L387: Tasks can also use another package for execution, for example when entering the shell:
L388: 
L389: devenv.nix
L390: 
L391:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L392: 
L393:     {
L394:       tasks = {
L395:         "python:hello" = {
L396:           exec = ''
L397:             print("Hello world from Python!")
L398:           '';
L399:           package = config.languages.python.package;
L400:         };
L401:       };
L402:     }
L403:     `
L404: ## Avoiding running expensive `exec` via `status` check
L405: 
L406: If you define a `status` command, it will be executed first and if it returns `0`, `exec` will be skipped.
L407: 
L408: devenv.nix
L409: 
L410:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L411: 
L412:     {
L413:       tasks = {
L414:         "myapp:migrations" = {
L415:           exec = "db-migrate";
L416:           status = "db-needs-migrations";
L417:         };
L418:       };
L419:     }
L420:     `
L421: Tasks using the `status` attribute will also cache their outputs. When a task is skipped because its status command returns success, the output from the most recent successful run will be restored and passed to dependent tasks.
L422: ## Executing tasks only when files have been modified
L423: 
L424: You can specify a list of files to monitor with `execIfModified`. The task will only run if any of these files have been modified since the last successful run. This attribute supports glob patterns, allowing you to monitor multiple files matching specific patterns.
L425: devenv.nix
L426: 
L427:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L428: 
L429:     {
L430:       tasks = {
L431:         "myapp:build" = {
L432:           exec = "npm run build";
L433:           execIfModified = [
L434:             "src/**/*.ts"  # All TypeScript files in src directory
L435:             "*.json"       # All JSON files in the current directory
L436:             "package.json" # Specific file
L437:             "src"          # Entire directory
L438:           ];
L439:           # Optionally run the build in a specific directory
L440:           cwd = "./frontend";
L441:         };
L442:       };
L443:     }
L444:     `
L445: This is particularly useful for tasks that depend on specific files and don't need to run if those files haven't changed.
L446: 
L447: The system tracks both file modification times and content hashes to detect actual changes. If a file's timestamp changes but its content remains the same (which can happen when touching a file or when saving without making changes), the task will be skipped.
L448: When a task is skipped due to no file changes, any previous outputs from that task are preserved and passed to dependent tasks, making the caching more efficient.
L449: ## Inputs / Outputs
L450: 
L451: Tasks support passing inputs and produce outputs, both as JSON objects:
L452:   * `$DEVENV_TASK_INPUT`: JSON object of `tasks."myapp:mytask".input`.
L453:   * `$DEVENV_TASKS_OUTPUTS`: JSON object with dependent tasks as keys and their outputs as values.
L454:   * `$DEVENV_TASK_OUTPUT_FILE`: a writable file with tasks' outputs in JSON.
L455:   * `$DEVENV_TASK_EXPORTS_FILE`: a writable file where tasks can export environment variables. Write `name\0base64(value)\0` pairs to this file and they will be set in the environment of dependent tasks.
L456: devenv.nix
L457: 
L458:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L459: 
L460:     {
L461:       tasks = {
L462:         "myapp:mytask" = {
L463:           exec = ''
L464:             echo $DEVENV_TASK_INPUT > $DEVENV_ROOT/input.json
L465:             echo '{ "output": 1 }' > $DEVENV_TASK_OUTPUT_FILE
L466:             echo $DEVENV_TASKS_OUTPUTS > $DEVENV_ROOT/outputs.json
L467:           '';
L468:           input = {
L469:             value = 1;
L470:           };
L471:         };
L472:       };
L473:     }
L474:     `
L475: ### Shell messages
L476: 
L477: New in version 2.1
L478: 
L479: Tasks can display messages to the user when entering the shell by writing a `devenv.messages` array to `$DEVENV_TASK_OUTPUT_FILE`. This is useful for showing informational output like trace URLs or setup status after initialization.
L480: devenv.nix
L481: 
L482:     `{ pkgs, lib, config, ... }:
L483: 
L484:     {
L485:       tasks = {
L486:         "myapp:info" = {
L487:           exec = ''
L488:             echo '{"devenv":{"messages":["Setup complete. Dashboard: http://localhost:3000"]}}' > "$DEVENV_TASK_OUTPUT_FILE"
L489:           '';
L490:           before = [ "devenv:enterShell" ];
L491:         };
L492:       };
L493:     }
L494:     `
L495: 
L496: Messages are printed after the shell environment is loaded, so they remain visible in the interactive session.
L497: ### Passing inputs from the CLI
L498: 
L499: New in version 2.0
L500: 
L501: You can override or add inputs when running tasks from the command line using `--input` and `--input-json`:
L502: 
L503:     `$ devenv tasks run myapp:mytask --input value=42 --input name=hello
L504:     `
L505: 
L506: Values are automatically parsed as JSON when valid, otherwise treated as strings. For example, `--input count=3` sets a number, `--input flag=true` sets a boolean, and `--input name=hello` sets a string.
L507: You can also pass a full JSON object:
L508: 
L509:     `$ devenv tasks run myapp:mytask --input-json '{"value": 42, "name": "hello"}'
L510:     `
L511: 
L512: Both flags can be combined. `--input-json` is applied first, then individual `--input` values are merged on top (CLI wins on conflict with Nix-defined inputs).
L513: ## Processes as tasks
L514: 
L515: Added in `1.4`
L516: 
L517: All processes defined in `processes` are automatically available as tasks with the `devenv:processes:` prefix. This allows you to:
L518: 
L519:   * Run individual processes as tasks
L520:   * Define dependencies between tasks and processes
L521:   * Use task features like `before`/`after` with processes
L522: devenv.nix
L523: 
L524:     `{ pkgs, ... }:
L525: 
L526:     {
L527:       # Define a process
L528:       processes.web-server = {
L529:         exec = "python -m http.server 8080";
L530:       };
L531: 
L532:       # Define a task that runs before the process
L533:       tasks."app:setup-data" = {
L534:         exec = "echo 'Setting up data...'";
L535:         before = [ "devenv:processes:web-server" ];
L536:       };
L537:     }
L538:     `
L539: When you run `devenv tasks run devenv:processes:web-server`, it will: 1. First run any tasks that have `before = [ "devenv:processes:web-server" ]` 2. Then execute the process itself
L540: 
L541: This is particularly useful for:
L542: 
L543:   * Running setup tasks before starting a process
L544:   * Creating complex startup sequences
L545:   * Testing individual processes without starting all of them
L546: You can also run tasks after a process finishes by depending on its `@completed` state (see cite138†Dependency states ). The default suffix for a process dependency is `@ready`, which fires as soon as the process is healthy, so use `@completed` to wait for it to exit instead:
L547: devenv.nix
L548: 
L549:     `{ pkgs, ... }:
L550: 
L551:     {
L552:       # Define an application server process
L553:       processes.app-server = {
L554:         exec = "node server.js";
L555:       };
L556: 
L557:       # Define a task that runs after the server stops
L558:       tasks."app:cleanup" = {
L559:         exec = ''
L560:           echo "Server stopped, cleaning up..."
L561:           rm -f ./server.pid
L562:           rm -rf ./tmp/cache/*
L563:         '';
L564:         after = [ "devenv:processes:app-server@completed" ];
L565:       };
L566:     }
L567:     `
L568: This ensures that cleanup tasks like removing PID files or clearing caches are executed when the application server stops.
L569: 
L570: Setup tasks attached to processes and `devenv up`
L571: A task that runs after a process — a setup or configure step wired with `processes.<name>.before = [ "devenv:<name>:configure" ]`, or equivalently `tasks."devenv:<name>:configure".after = [ "devenv:processes:<name>" ]` — is downstream of that process. `devenv up` schedules processes in `before` mode, which runs each process's upstream dependencies but not its downstream tasks, so the setup step is skipped and never runs.
L572: Until this is resolved (cite192†#2852†github.com ), run `devenv up --mode all` to include downstream setup tasks. `devenv test` already runs in `all` mode, so these tasks run there. See cite139†Execution modes .
L573: ## Git Integration
L574: 
L575: Added in `1.10`
L576: 
L577: Tasks can reference the git repository root path using `${config.git.root}`, which is particularly useful in monorepo environments:
L578: 
L579: devenv.nix
L580: 
L581:     `{ config, ... }:
L582: 
L583:     {
L584:       tasks."build:frontend" = {
L585:         exec = "npm run build";
L586:         cwd = "${config.git.root}/frontend";
L587:       };
L588: 
L589:       tasks."test:backend" = {
L590:         exec = "cargo test";
L591:         cwd = "${config.git.root}/backend";
L592:       };
L593:     }
L594:     `
L595: This allows tasks to reference paths relative to the repository root regardless of where the `devenv.nix` file is located within the repository.
L596: ## SDK using Task Server Protocol
L597: 
L598: See cite193†Task Server Protocol†github.com for a proposal how defining tasks in your favorite language would look like.
